raw: CHAPTER V. The Wood-Sawyer
en: [Chapter 5] The Wood-Sawyer

raw: One year and three months.
en: One year and three months passed.

raw: During all that time Lucie was never sure, from hour to hour, but that the Guillotine would strike off her husband’s head next day.
en: During all that time, Lucie was never sure from one hour to the next whether the Guillotine would cut off her husband's head the following day.

raw: Every day, through the stony streets, the tumbrils now jolted heavily, filled with Condemned.
en: Every day, heavy carts rumbled through the cobblestone streets, packed with condemned prisoners.

raw: Lovely girls; bright women, brown-haired, black-haired, and grey; youths; stalwart men and old; gentle born and peasant born; all red wine for La Guillotine, all daily brought into light from the dark cellars of the loathsome prisons, and carried to her through the streets to slake her devouring thirst.
en: Beautiful girls, young women, dark-haired, brown-haired, and gray-haired women, boys, strong men, and the elderly, aristocrats and peasants alike, were all food for the Guillotine. They were brought daily from the dark cells of the filthy prisons and carried through the streets to satisfy its endless thirst.

raw: Liberty, equality, fraternity, or death;--the last, much the easiest to bestow, O Guillotine!
en: Liberty, equality, fraternity, or death, and death was by far the easiest for the Guillotine to give!

raw: If the suddenness of her calamity, and the whirling wheels of the time, had stunned the Doctor’s daughter into awaiting the result in idle despair, it would but have been with her as it was with many.
en: If the sudden shock of this disaster and the chaotic pace of the times had caused the Doctor's daughter to give up in despair, she would have been just like many others.

raw: But, from the hour when she had taken the white head to her fresh young bosom in the garret of Saint Antoine, she had been true to her duties.
en: But ever since the day she had held her father's white-haired head in the attic of Saint Antoine, she had always done her duty.

raw: She was truest to them in the season of trial, as all the quietly loyal and good will always be.
en: She was most loyal during this time of trial, just as all good and quiet people are.

raw: As soon as they were established in their new residence, and her father had entered on the routine of his avocations, she arranged the little household as exactly as if her husband had been there.
en: As soon as they moved into their new apartment and her father began his daily routine, she organized the household exactly as if Charles were there.

raw: Everything had its appointed place and its appointed time.
en: Everything had its place and time.

raw: Little Lucie she taught, as regularly, as if they had all been united in their English home.
en: She taught little Lucie as regularly as if they were still in their peaceful English home.

raw: The slight devices with which she cheated herself into the show of a belief that they would soon be reunited--the little preparations for his speedy return, the setting aside of his chair and his books--these, and the solemn prayer at night for one dear prisoner especially, among the many unhappy souls in prison and the shadow of death--were almost the only outspoken reliefs of her heavy mind.
en: The small tricks she played on herself to pretend they would soon be together again, like setting aside his chair and books for his return, and praying at night for her dear prisoner among the many suffering in the shadow of death, were the only ways she could find relief for her heavy heart.

raw: She did not greatly alter in appearance.
en: She did not change much in appearance.

raw: The plain dark dresses, akin to mourning dresses, which she and her child wore, were as neat and as well attended to as the brighter clothes of happy days.
en: The simple dark dresses, almost like mourning clothes, that she and her child wore were as neat and clean as their colorful clothes from happier days.

raw: She lost her colour, and the old and intent expression was a constant, not an occasional, thing; otherwise, she remained very pretty and comely.
en: She lost some of her color, and her worried, serious expression was now permanent, but otherwise she remained very pretty.

raw: Sometimes, at night on kissing her father, she would burst into the grief she had repressed all day, and would say that her sole reliance, under Heaven, was on him.
en: Sometimes at night, when kissing her father goodnight, she would cry and let out the grief she had hidden all day, telling him he was her only hope.

raw: He always resolutely answered: “Nothing can happen to him without my knowledge, and I know that I can save him, Lucie.”
en: He always answered firmly, “Nothing can happen to him without my knowing, and I know I can save him, Lucie.”

raw: They had not made the round of their changed life many weeks, when her father said to her, on coming home one evening:
en: They had only lived this way for a few weeks when her father said to her one evening upon coming home:

raw: “My dear, there is an upper window in the prison, to which Charles can sometimes gain access at three in the afternoon.
en: “My dear, there is a high window in the prison that Charles can sometimes reach at three in the afternoon.

raw: When he can get to it--which depends on many uncertainties and incidents--he might see you in the street, he thinks, if you stood in a certain place that I can show you.
en: When he can get to it, which depends on many things, he thinks he might be able to see you in the street if you stand in a specific spot I can show you.

raw: But you will not be able to see him, my poor child, and even if you could, it would be unsafe for you to make a sign of recognition.”
en: But you won't be able to see him, my poor child, and even if you could, it would be unsafe to wave or show that you recognize him.”

raw: “O show me the place, my father, and I will go there every day.”
en: “Oh, show me the place, Father, and I will go there every day.”

raw: From that time, in all weathers, she waited there two hours.
en: From then on, in all kinds of weather, she waited there for two hours.

raw: As the clock struck two, she was there, and at four she turned resignedly away.
en: She arrived at two o'clock and left at four.

raw: When it was not too wet or inclement for her child to be with her, they went together; at other times she was alone; but, she never missed a single day.
en: When it was not too wet or cold for her daughter, they went together; other times she went alone, but she never missed a day.

raw: It was the dark and dirty corner of a small winding street.
en: The spot was a dark, dirty corner of a narrow, winding street.

raw: The hovel of a cutter of wood into lengths for burning, was the only house at that end; all else was wall.
en: The shack of a wood-sawyer was the only building there; everything else was just a high wall.

raw: On the third day of her being there, he noticed her.
en: On her third day of waiting there, he noticed her.

raw: “Good day, citizeness.”
en: “Good day, citizeness.”

raw: “Good day, citizen.”
en: “Good day, citizen.”

raw: This mode of address was now prescribed by decree.
en: This way of greeting was now required by law.

raw: It had been established voluntarily some time ago, among the more thorough patriots; but, was now law for everybody.
en: It had started voluntarily among the most loyal patriots, but now everyone had to use it.

raw: “Walking here again, citizeness?”
en: “Walking here again, citizeness?”

raw: “You see me, citizen!”
en: “You see me, citizen!”

raw: The wood-sawyer, who was a little man with a redundancy of gesture (he had once been a mender of roads), cast a glance at the prison, pointed at the prison, and putting his ten fingers before his face to represent bars, peeped through them jocosely.
en: The wood-sawyer was a small man who made a lot of gestures, he was the same man who had once been the road-mender. He looked at the prison, pointed to it, and held up his ten fingers like bars, joking as he peeked through them.

raw: “But it’s not my business,” said he. And went on sawing his wood.
en: “But it's none of my business,” he said, and went back to sawing his wood.

raw: Next day he was looking out for her, and accosted her the moment she appeared.
en: The next day, he was watching for her and spoke to her the moment she arrived.

raw: “What?
en: “What?

raw: Walking here again, citizeness?”
en: Walking here again, citizeness?”

raw: “Yes, citizen.”
en: “Yes, citizen.”

raw: “Ah!
en: “Ah!

raw: A child too!
en: A child too!

raw: Your mother, is it not, my little citizeness?”
en: That is your mother, isn't it, my little citizeness?”

raw: “Do I say yes, mamma?” whispered little Lucie, drawing close to her.
en: “Should I say yes, Mama?” whispered little Lucie, holding close to her.

raw: “Yes, dearest.”
en: “Yes, dearest.”

raw: “Yes, citizen.”
en: “Yes, citizen.”

raw: “Ah!
en: “Ah!

raw: But it’s not my business.
en: But it's none of my business.

raw: My work is my business.
en: My work is my business.

raw: See my saw!
en: Look at my saw!

raw: I call it my Little Guillotine.
en: I call it my Little Guillotine.

raw: La, la, la; La, la, la!
en: La, la, la; La, la, la!

raw: And off his head comes!”
en: And off his head comes!”

raw: The billet fell as he spoke, and he threw it into a basket.
en: A log fell as he spoke, and he tossed it into a basket.

raw: “I call myself the Samson of the firewood guillotine.
en: “I call myself the executioner Samson of the firewood guillotine.

raw: See here again!
en: Look here again!

raw: Loo, loo, loo; Loo, loo, loo!
en: Loo, loo, loo; Loo, loo, loo!

raw: And off _her_ head comes!
en: And off _her_ head comes!

raw: Now, a child.
en: Now, a child.

raw: Tickle, tickle; Pickle, pickle!
en: Tickle, tickle; Pickle, pickle!

raw: And off _its_ head comes.
en: And off _its_ head comes.

raw: All the family!”
en: The whole family!”

raw: Lucie shuddered as he threw two more billets into his basket, but it was impossible to be there while the wood-sawyer was at work, and not be in his sight.
en: Lucie shivered as he threw two more logs into his basket, but she couldn't stand there without being in his sight.

raw: Thenceforth, to secure his good will, she always spoke to him first, and often gave him drink-money, which he readily received.
en: From then on, to keep him friendly, she always spoke to him first and often gave him tip money, which he was happy to take.

raw: He was an inquisitive fellow, and sometimes when she had quite forgotten him in gazing at the prison roof and grates, and in lifting her heart up to her husband, she would come to herself to find him looking at her, with his knee on his bench and his saw stopped in its work. “But it’s not my business!” he would generally say at those times, and would briskly fall to his sawing again.
en: He was very curious, and sometimes when she had forgotten all about him while staring up at the prison roof and praying for her husband, she would look over to find him watching her, with his knee on his bench and his saw stopped. “But it's none of my business!” he would usually say, and then start sawing again.

raw: In all weathers, in the snow and frost of winter, in the bitter winds of spring, in the hot sunshine of summer, in the rains of autumn, and again in the snow and frost of winter, Lucie passed two hours of every day at this place; and every day on leaving it, she kissed the prison wall.
en: Through snow, winter frost, bitter spring winds, hot summer sun, and autumn rain, Lucie spent two hours there every day. Every day, as she left, she kissed the prison wall.

raw: Her husband saw her (so she learned from her father) it might be once in five or six times: it might be twice or thrice running: it might be, not for a week or a fortnight together.
en: Her husband saw her, according to her father, maybe once every five or six times, sometimes twice in a row, and sometimes not for weeks.

raw: It was enough that he could and did see her when the chances served, and on that possibility she would have waited out the day, seven days a week.
en: Knowing that he could see her when he had the chance was enough, and for that possibility she would have stood there all day, seven days a week.

raw: These occupations brought her round to the December month, wherein her father walked among the terrors with a steady head.
en: These daily visits brought her to the month of December, when her father was working calmly amid the city's terrors.

raw: On a lightly-snowing afternoon she arrived at the usual corner.
en: One snowy afternoon, she arrived at her usual corner.

raw: It was a day of some wild rejoicing, and a festival.
en: It was a day of celebration.

raw: She had seen the houses, as she came along, decorated with little pikes, and with little red caps stuck upon them; also, with tricoloured ribbons; also, with the standard inscription (tricoloured letters were the favourite), Republic One and Indivisible.
en: As she walked, she had seen houses decorated with small toy spears, red caps, tri-color ribbons, and the slogan written in red, white, and blue: "Republic One and Indivisible.

raw: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death!
en: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death!"

raw: The miserable shop of the wood-sawyer was so small, that its whole surface furnished very indifferent space for this legend.
en: The wood-sawyer's tiny shop was too small to fit the long slogan easily.

raw: He had got somebody to scrawl it up for him, however, who had squeezed Death in with most inappropriate difficulty.
en: He had paid someone to paint it for him, and they had squeezed the word "Death" onto the end with great difficulty.

raw: On his house-top, he displayed pike and cap, as a good citizen must, and in a window he had stationed his saw inscribed as his “Little Sainte Guillotine”--for the great sharp female was by that time popularly canonised.
en: On his roof, he displayed a toy spear and cap like a good citizen, and in the window he kept his saw labeled "Little Saint Guillotine", since the crowd now spoke of the machine as if it were a saint.

raw: His shop was shut and he was not there, which was a relief to Lucie, and left her quite alone.
en: His shop was closed and he was gone, which was a relief to Lucie, leaving her alone.

raw: But, he was not far off, for presently she heard a troubled movement and a shouting coming along, which filled her with fear.
en: But he wasn't far away. Soon enough, she heard a chaotic commotion and loud shouting coming down the street, which filled her with fear.

raw: A moment afterwards, and a throng of people came pouring round the corner by the prison wall, in the midst of whom was the wood-sawyer hand in hand with The Vengeance.
en: A moment later, a massive crowd of people came pouring around the corner by the prison wall, and right in the middle of them was the wood-sawyer, holding hands with The Vengeance.

raw: There could not be fewer than five hundred people, and they were dancing like five thousand demons.
en: A moment later, a mob of people came rushing around the corner.

raw: There was no other music than their own singing.
en: In the middle of them was the wood-sawyer, holding hands with The Vengeance.

raw: They danced to the popular Revolution song, keeping a ferocious time that was like a gnashing of teeth in unison.
en: There were at least five hundred people, dancing like demons.

raw: Men and women danced together, women danced together, men danced together, as hazard had brought them together.
en: They had no music other than their own singing, chanting the popular revolutionary song to a fierce rhythm that sounded like the grinding of teeth.

raw: At first, they were a mere storm of coarse red caps and coarse woollen rags; but, as they filled the place, and stopped to dance about Lucie, some ghastly apparition of a dance-figure gone raving mad arose among them.
en: At first, they just looked like a wild storm of rough red caps and coarse wool rags. But as they filled the square and stopped to dance around Lucie, they looked like a terrifying, ghostly dance that had gone completely mad.

raw: They advanced, retreated, struck at one another’s hands, clutched at one another’s heads, spun round alone, caught one another and spun round in pairs, until many of them dropped.
en: They moved forward and backward, smacked each other's hands, grabbed at each other's heads, spun around on their own, and grabbed each other to spin in pairs until many of them collapsed.

raw: While those were down, the rest linked hand in hand, and all spun round together: then the ring broke, and in separate rings of two and four they turned and turned until they all stopped at once, began again, struck, clutched, and tore, and then reversed the spin, and all spun round another way.
en: While some lay on the ground, the rest linked hands and spun around together. Then the big circle broke apart into smaller rings of two or four, and they kept spinning until they all stopped at the same time. They started up again—hitting, grabbing, and tearing at each other—before reversing direction and spinning the opposite way.

raw: Suddenly they stopped again, paused, struck out the time afresh, formed into lines the width of the public way, and, with their heads low down and their hands high up, swooped screaming off. No fight could have been half so terrible as this dance.
en: Then they broke into smaller groups, spinning faster and faster, before suddenly stopping, forming a line across the street, and running off screaming.

raw: It was so emphatically a fallen sport--a something, once innocent, delivered over to all devilry--a healthy pastime changed into a means of angering the blood, bewildering the senses, and steeling the heart.
en: It was clearly a ruined activity—something that was once innocent, but had now been handed over to pure evil. A healthy pastime had been twisted into a way to boil the blood, confuse the senses, and harden the heart.

raw: Such grace as was visible in it, made it the uglier, showing how warped and perverted all things good by nature were become.
en: It was the Carmagnole, a once-innocent pastime now turned into a ritual of anger and madness.

raw: The maidenly bosom bared to this, the pretty almost-child’s head thus distracted, the delicate foot mincing in this slough of blood and dirt, were types of the disjointed time.
en: Its wild, dark energy showed how twisted the country had become, with young women and girls caught up in this dirty, bloody display.

raw: This was the Carmagnole.
en: This was the Carmagnole dance.

raw: As it passed, leaving Lucie frightened and bewildered in the doorway of the wood-sawyer’s house, the feathery snow fell as quietly and lay as white and soft, as if it had never been.
en: As it moved away, leaving Lucie frightened and confused in the doorway of the wood-sawyer's shop, the light snow fell quietly and lay white and soft, as if nothing had happened.

raw: “O my father!” for he stood before her when she lifted up the eyes she had momentarily darkened with her hand; “such a cruel, bad sight.”
en: “Oh, Father!” she said when she looked up and saw him standing there. “It was such a cruel, horrible sight.”

raw: “I know, my dear, I know.
en: “I know, my dear, I know.

raw: I have seen it many times.
en: I have seen it many times.

raw: Don’t be frightened!
en: Don't be scared!

raw: Not one of them would harm you.”
en: None of them would hurt you.”

raw: “I am not frightened for myself, my father.
en: “I am not afraid for myself, Father.

raw: But when I think of my husband, and the mercies of these people--”
en: But when I think of my husband, and the mercy of these people, ”

raw: “We will set him above their mercies very soon.
en: “We will save him from them very soon.

raw: I left him climbing to the window, and I came to tell you.
en: I left him climbing to the window, and I came to tell you.

raw: There is no one here to see.
en: No one is watching.

raw: You may kiss your hand towards that highest shelving roof.”
en: You can blow a kiss toward that high roof.”

raw: “I do so, father, and I send him my Soul with it!”
en: “I am doing it, Father, and I send him my soul with it!”

raw: “You cannot see him, my poor dear?”
en: “You can't see him, my poor child?”

raw: “No, father,” said Lucie, yearning and weeping as she kissed her hand, “no.”
en: “No, Father,” Lucie said, crying as she blew a kiss, “no.”

raw: A footstep in the snow.
en: A footstep sounded in the snow.

raw: Madame Defarge. “I salute you, citizeness,”  from the Doctor. “I salute you, citizen.” This in passing.
en: It was Madame Defarge. “Greetings, citizeness,” said the Doctor. “Greetings, citizen,” she replied as she walked by.

raw: Nothing more.
en: Nothing more.

raw: Madame Defarge gone, like a shadow over the white road.
en: Madame Defarge vanished like a shadow over the white road.

raw: “Give me your arm, my love.
en: “Take my arm, my love.

raw: Pass from here with an air of cheerfulness and courage, for his sake.
en: Walk away from here looking cheerful and brave, for his sake.

raw: That was well done;” they had left the spot; “it shall not be in vain.
en: That's it,” he said as they left the corner. “It won't be in vain.

raw: Charles is summoned for to-morrow.”
en: Charles is summoned for trial tomorrow.”

raw: “For to-morrow!”
en: “For tomorrow!”

raw: “There is no time to lose.
en: “There is no time to lose.

raw: I am well prepared, but there are precautions to be taken, that could not be taken until he was actually summoned before the Tribunal.
en: I am well prepared, but there are steps we have to take that we couldn't take until he was actually summoned.

raw: He has not received the notice yet, but I know that he will presently be summoned for to-morrow, and removed to the Conciergerie; I have timely information.
en: He hasn't received the notice yet, but I know he will be called tomorrow and moved to the Conciergerie prison. I got the information early.

raw: You are not afraid?”
en: You are not afraid, are you?”

raw: She could scarcely answer, “I trust in you.”
en: She could barely reply, “I trust you.”

raw: “Do so, implicitly.
en: “Trust me completely.

raw: Your suspense is nearly ended, my darling; he shall be restored to you within a few hours; I have encompassed him with every protection.
en: The waiting is almost over, my darling. He will be back with you in a few hours. I have arranged every protection for him.

raw: I must see Lorry.”
en: I must see Lorry.”

raw: He stopped.
en: He stopped.

raw: There was a heavy lumbering of wheels within hearing.
en: They heard the heavy rumble of wheels nearby.

raw: They both knew too well what it meant.
en: They both knew exactly what it meant.

raw: One.
en: One.

raw: Two.
en: Two.

raw: Three.
en: Three.

raw: Three tumbrils faring away with their dread loads over the hushing snow.
en: Three carts carrying their terrible loads away over the silent snow.

raw: “I must see Lorry,” the Doctor repeated, turning her another way.
en: “I must see Lorry,” the Doctor repeated, leading her down another street.

raw: The staunch old gentleman was still in his trust; had never left it.
en: The loyal old gentleman was still working at his post.

raw: He and his books were in frequent requisition as to property confiscated and made national.
en: He and his records were often consulted by the government regarding seized property.

raw: What he could save for the owners, he saved.
en: Whatever he could save for the bank's customers, he saved.

raw: No better man living to hold fast by what Tellson’s had in keeping, and to hold his peace.
en: There was no better man to guard Tellson's assets and keep his mouth shut.

raw: A murky red and yellow sky, and a rising mist from the Seine, denoted the approach of darkness.
en: A cloudy red and yellow sky and mist rising from the Seine River showed that night was falling.

raw: It was almost dark when they arrived at the Bank.
en: It was almost dark when they reached the bank.

raw: The stately residence of Monseigneur was altogether blighted and deserted.
en: The lord's grand house was completely ruined and empty.

raw: Above a heap of dust and ashes in the court, ran the letters: National Property.
en: Above a pile of dust and ashes in the yard, painted letters read: "National Property.

raw: Republic One and Indivisible.
en: Republic One and Indivisible.

raw: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death!
en: Liberty, Equality, Fraternity, or Death!"

raw: Who could that be with Mr.
en: Who could that be with Mr.

raw: Lorry--the owner of the riding-coat upon the chair--who must not be seen?
en: Lorry, the owner of the coat sitting on the chair, who had to remain hidden?

raw: From whom newly arrived, did he come out, agitated and surprised, to take his favourite in his arms?
en: From which newly arrived traveler did Mr. Lorry come out, excited and surprised, to hug Lucie?

raw: To whom did he appear to repeat her faltering words, when, raising his voice and turning his head towards the door of the room from which he had issued, he said: “Removed to the Conciergerie, and summoned for to-morrow?”
en: To whom was he repeating her worried words when he raised his voice, looked back toward the closed door of the private room, and said: “Moved to the Conciergerie, and summoned for trial tomorrow?”
